name: Co-living
summary: Purpose-built co-living: private furnished bedrooms (often with private bath) clustered in suites around shared kitchens and lounges, leased by the room, usually urban podium or mid-rise. Structure costs follow podium multifamily; per-bed cost is driven by gross SF per bed (~300-350), bathroom density and furnishing. No public US per-bed construction budget was found in this pass, so all cost values are derived from the multifamily files and should be verified.

typicalSize.method: Typical new-build US co-living projects ~100-450 bedrooms (e.g., Boston Allston co-living building with 279 bedrooms, e6; judgment).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross SF per bed: private bedroom 130-200 SF (+ ~40-50 SF private bath where provided) plus ~60-100 SF/bed of shared kitchen/lounge, and corridors/amenity at ~80% efficiency => ~280-400. Compare Census median new rental unit 1,000 SF (e4).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Podium/mid-rise density (~80-150 units/acre, see podium-multifamily.json) at ~2.5-3 beds per equivalent unit.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Co-living is typically sited near transit with reduced or no parking (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: perSF x sfPerPrimaryUnit: mid $300 x 330 = ~$100k/bed; low ~$230 x 280 = ~$65k (wood mid-rise, shared baths); high ~$410 x 400 = ~$165k (high-rise, private baths).

perSF.method: Derived: podium multifamily mid $290/SF (podium-multifamily.json; LandSouth podium $235-350, e2; RSMeans 4-7 story $210-475, e3; RLB 18-city multifamily median $225-410, e1) + ~3% for higher bathroom density and suite kitchens per SF; high = high-rise mid ($410).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions, OH&P and on-site work; excludes land, soft costs, room/common furniture (FF&E line), off-sites, impact/tap fees, financing. Parking, if any, via the podium file's parking items. Conversions of offices/hotels are not represented.

qualityTiers.method: Same tier steps as podium multifamily (see podium-multifamily.json).

systemSplit.method: Derived from the podium split in this category: +1.2 pts plumbing (22, bath per bedroom), +0.5 finishes (09), +0.5 HVAC (23), +0.3 low-voltage (27, room access/Wi-Fi); offset by fewer in-unit kitchens (-0.8 equipment 11, -0.7 casework 12) and less parking concrete (-1.0 03); 01 absorbs rounding.

cost.method: Derived: larger-than-apartment kitchen with multiple refrigerators/storage, appliances and casework (2026 judgment).
Derived: compact bathroom incl. fixtures, tile, rough-in (2026 judgment); ~80% of new-build co-living rooms have private baths (assumption).

lineItems.name: Room-level smart locks and managed Wi-Fi

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: furnished bedroom plus share of shared kitchen smallwares, lounge and co-working furniture (2026 judgment); co-living is leased fully furnished.

pctOfHard.method: Derived: RAND market-rate soft/hard 0.19-0.33 incl. financing (e5); urban podium-like entitlement plus operator/brand technical services; mid 0.25 excluding construction interest.

softCosts.notes: Zoning often treats co-living as a special use (SRO/rooming house/group living) - entitlement risk and time can add soft cost.

design.method: Derived: newer building type with code-interpretation risk.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $65k x 1.15 ~= $75k; hard high $165k x 1.45 ~= $240k.

evidence.region: Median of the 18 US cities in RLB's table

source.title: RLB Construction Cost Report North America Q3 2026 (PDF), Indicative Construction Costs table

evidence.quote: Indicative Construction Costs table, Residential 'Multi-Family' column (US$/SF GFA), 18 US cities from Austin 190-285 to San Francisco 420-700; median LOW 225, median HIGH 410 (computed from the table)
evidence.scopeNotes: RLB: 'Values of U.S. locations represent hard construction costs based on U.S. dollars per square foot of gross floor area.' One 'Multi-Family' column covers all multifamily product (garden to high-rise); sitework treatment not stated. Median of city lows/highs computed by the researcher; the 18 cities skew to large, higher-cost metros.

source.title: Which multifamily product type is right for your site

evidence.quote: Wrap ... $200 to $275 per square foot; Podium ... at current industry hard costs near $235 to $350 per square foot
evidence.scopeNotes: Multifamily product-type ranges used as a proxy - new-build co-living is typically podium or mid-rise.

source.title: How Much Does It Cost to Build an Apartment Complex?

evidence.scopeNotes: RSMeans square-foot model range (4-7 story apartment); page calls it a national average; scope (sitework, soft) not stated. Page dated May 29, 2026 but headed '2025 Guide' - treated as 2025 dollars.

evidence.quote: The median size of multifamily units completed that were built for rent was 1,000 square feet
evidence.scopeNotes: All new multifamily rental units completed in 2025 (all building types); net unit area.

source.title: The High Cost of Producing Multifamily Housing in California (RAND RR-A3743-1, Ward & Schlake, 2025) - copy hosted by San Diego Housing Commission

evidence.quote: Table 3.1 Panel C. Soft Costs: Texas Market rate $22; Colorado Market rate $44; California Market rate $84 (vs Panel A hard costs $115 / $237 / $253 per NRSF)
evidence.scopeNotes: Soft/hard ratios derived: TX 0.19, CO 0.19, CA 0.33. RAND soft costs include A&E, legal, fees and financing costs; market-rate sample mixes garden, podium, wrap, high-rise.

source.title: Allston development gets $58M financing after fast lease-up (Nov 19, 2024)

evidence.quote: The 525 LINK contains 279 bedrooms, most of them located in suites sharing living and dining areas.
evidence.scopeNotes: Project-size data point only (co-living with some conventional apartments); the $58M is permanent financing, not cost.

openQuestions: No US co-living project budget with construction cost per bedroom was found (searched developer press, Boston/LA trade coverage); a city staff report or lender disclosure would anchor this file.
Share of rooms with private baths and beds per kitchen vary by operator - confirm design assumptions.
Office/hotel-to-co-living conversions need a separate cost basis.
